project-charter.title: 1. Engineering Problem Charter & Technical Scope

cards.title: Automotive Engineering Scenario & Power Transmission Brief
cards.body:
You act as a Mechanical Transmission Design Engineer investigating the reverse gear mechanism of a passenger-car manual transmission. The transmission kinematic arrangement is:
• Engine / Input Shaft (N1 = 1200 rpm, P = 8.0 kW)
  ↓
• Reverse Driving Spur Gear (Pinion, z1 = 20 teeth)
  ↓
• Reverse Idler Gear (Direction Inverter, z_idler teeth)
  ↓
• Reverse Driven Spur Gear (Output Gear, z2 = 60 teeth, N2 = 400 rpm)
  ↓
• Output Shaft to Final Drive

The reverse idler changes the direction of rotation to achieve reverse vehicle motion, but does not alter the transmission speed ratio (i = N1 / N2 = 3.00). The student must verify whether the selected spur-gear pair is structurally and tribologically adequate.

cards.title: Central Engineering Question & Technical Scope
cards.body:
Central Engineering Question:
"Can the selected spur-gear pair safely transmit the required power and torque without bending or wear failure, and what engineering modification should be recommended if a criterion is not satisfied?"

Technical Specifications (Frozen Dataset):
• Transmitted Power: P = 8.0 kW
• Input Pinion Speed: N1 = 1200 rpm
• Output Gear Speed: N2 = 400 rpm (Ratio i = 3.00)
• Tooth Numbers: Pinion z1 = 20, Gear z2 = 60
• Standard Module: m = 3.0 mm, Face Width: b = 50.0 mm
• Pressure Angle: phi = 20° Full-Depth Involute
• Service Factor: Cs = 1.50, Load Concentration Factor: Km = 1.25
• Target Safety Factor: [FOS] = 1.50
• Pinion Material: Sut1 = 700 MPa, Surface Hardness = 350 BHN
• Gear Material: Sut2 = 600 MPa, Surface Hardness = 350 BHN
• SPPU Syllabus Boundary: Unit I — Spur and Helical Gears (No numerical on force analysis of helical).

cards.title: Engineering Responsibility & Failure Mode Implications
cards.body: In automotive transmission systems, reverse gear trains experience severe shock torques during vehicle maneuvering and clutch engagement. Tooth bending fatigue failure leads to instantaneous tooth shearing, immobilizing the vehicle. In contrast, surface fatigue (wear and pitting) causes progressive tooth spalling, severe whine noise, and loss of involute profile conjugate action. The design engineer must evaluate both Lewis beam strength and Buckingham wear durability against the authoritative target [FOS] = 1.50.

project-charter.acceptanceText: I confirm my technical role as Mechanical Transmission Design Engineer. I acknowledge the automotive reverse spur gear problem charter, the SPPU PCC353-MEC syllabus boundary, and will evaluate tooth beam strength, wear durability, and redesign recommendations under CO1.

lewis-beam-strength.title: 6. Lewis Beam Strength & Bending Safety Factor
lewis-beam-strength.figure: Lewis Tooth Beam Strength & Weaker Element Determination
lewis-beam-strength.description: Determine permissible bending stresses, evaluate Lewis form factors, identify the weaker element, and compute Lewis beam strength and bending factor of safety.
given: Standard Module: m = 3.0 mm, Face Width: b = 50.0 mm
Factor of Safety on Sut: 3.00 (sigma_b = Sut / 3)

fields.label: Weaker Element Governing Bending Design
fields.hint: Pinion index = 74.67 MPa < Gear index = 84.20 MPa -> Pinion is weaker

buckingham-wear-analysis.figure: Buckingham Wear Durability & Surface Contact Fatigue

failure-diagnosis.title: 8. Automotive Failure Diagnosis & Governing Criterion
failure-diagnosis.prompt: Evaluate the calculated factors of safety (FOSb = 1.729 vs FOSw = 1.361 against target [FOS] = 1.50) to determine the governing failure mode.
failure-diagnosis.description: Synthesize structural and tribological results to diagnose the governing mechanical defect.
given: Wear Factor of Safety: FOSw = 1.361 < 1.50 (NOT SAFE)

mcq.question: Comparing the bending factor of safety (FOSb = 1.729) and wear factor of safety (FOSw = 1.361) against target [FOS] = 1.50, what is the governing failure diagnosis?

options.label: Bending strength is safe (FOSb = 1.729 >= 1.50), but wear durability is not safe (FOSw = 1.361 < 1.50). Therefore, surface wear / pitting fatigue governs the transmission design.
Tooth root bending fracture governs the design because the pinion is the weaker member; surface wear is fully satisfactory.
Both bending and wear durability criteria are completely satisfied; no potential failure mode exists.
Both bending and wear criteria fail catastrophically under reverse operating torque.

gear-adequacy-assessment.title: 9. Gear Adequacy Assessment & Engineering Decision
gear-adequacy-assessment.prompt: Make the deterministic engineering decision regarding the overall adequacy of the initial spur-gear pair for passenger car reverse transmission.
gear-adequacy-assessment.description: Synthesize design compliance against target standards and determine whether initial design approval can be granted.
given: Initial Gear Set: m = 3 mm, b = 50 mm, 350 BHN, a = 120 mm

mcq.question: What is the final deterministic engineering decision regarding the adequacy of the initial spur-gear pair in this automotive transmission?

options.label: The overall initial design is NOT ADEQUATE because the wear factor of safety (FOSw = 1.361) falls below the target factor of safety (1.50). An engineering modification is required.
The overall initial design is ADEQUATE because bending strength is safe and reverse gear operates only intermittently.
The overall initial design is CONDITIONALLY ACCEPTABLE without any engineering modification.
The design cannot be assessed without performing helical force calculations.

engineering-recommendation.title: 10. Engineering Recommendation & Redesign Defense
engineering-recommendation.description: Evaluate and defend engineering modifications to bring wear factor of safety above target [FOS] >= 1.50. You may verify the authoritative surface hardening pathway (Gear BHN = 400) or defend an alternative engineering solution.
given: Initial Baseline: Sw = 8,820 N, Peff = 6,478.87 N, FOSw = 1.361 (UNSAFE < 1.50)
Authoritative Redesign Option: Surface Hardening to 400 BHN (K = 2.56 N/mm², Sw = 11,520 N, FOSw = 1.778 >= 1.50)
Alternative Redesign Option A: Face width enlargement to b = 60 mm (Sw = 10,584 N, FOSw = 1.633 >= 1.50)
Alternative Redesign Option B: Module modification with altered pitch diameter & centre distance
Automotive Packaging Constraint: Preserving transmission casing envelope and centre distance a = 120 mm is highly desirable

fields.label: Selected Engineering Redesign Direction
options: Option 1: Surface Hardening to 400 BHN (K = 2.56 N/mm², Sw = 11,520 N, FOSw = 1.778 >= 1.50, preserves a = 120 mm)
Option 2: Increase Face Width to b = 60 mm (Sw = 10,584 N, FOSw = 1.633 >= 1.50, minor casing length growth)
Option 3: Module Enlargement to m = 3.5 mm (alters pitch diameter and casing centre distance)
Option 4: Combined Optimization (Surface Hardening + Synthetic High-EP Lubrication)
fields.hint: Select your recommended engineering modification for automotive implementation.

fields.label: Packaging & Casing Envelope Defense
fields.placeholder: Explain how your recommendation affects gearbox casing dimensions, shaft centre distance (a = 120 mm), and transmission compartment packaging...
fields.hint: Surface hardening preserves existing a = 120 mm; face width or module increases alter casting dimensions.

fields.label: Manufacturing Feasibility & Cost Justification
fields.placeholder: Defend heat treatment feasibility (induction / case carburizing to 400 BHN) vs retooling costs for module/casing changes...
fields.hint: Discuss induction hardening, distortion control, and economic trade-offs.

questions.label: Synthesis of Calculated Conclusions & Automotive Reverse Duty Cycle (TS04-C11 — 0.5 Marks)
questions.helpText: Synthesize the calculated parameters (T1 = 63,661.98 N·mm, Pt = 2122.07 N, Peff = 6478.87 N, FOSb = 1.729, FOSw = 1.361). Discuss why reverse gear trains operate under severe shock torques despite lower cumulative operating hours.
questions.placeholder: Synthesize your calculated findings. Address why reverse gear in a manual transmission experiences high shock loads during vehicle engagement and maneuvering, and explain how the intermediate idler gear functions kinematically without altering the 3:1 transmission ratio...

questions.label: Root Bending Fatigue vs Flank Pitting Contact Fatigue Mechanics (TS04-C11 — 0.5 Marks)
questions.helpText: Compare catastrophic tooth root bending fracture (governed by Lewis equation) against progressive pitch-line contact fatigue / pitting (governed by Buckingham equation). Explain why wear durability governed this automotive design.
questions.placeholder: Contrast the mechanics of root bending stress (tensile cyclic bending leading to rapid tooth fracture) with Hertzian contact stress on tooth flanks (cyclic compressive shear leading to microscopic subsurface microcracks and pit formation). Explain why the initial 350 BHN gear set provided safe bending (FOS = 1.729) but unsafe wear durability (FOS = 1.361)...

questions.label: Engineering Trade-Offs in Automotive Gearbox Casing Constraints (TS04-C11 — 0.5 Marks)
questions.helpText: Reflect on why increasing tooth surface hardness to 400 BHN is preferred in passenger car packaging over module enlargement or large face width increases. Address manufacturing, weight, and tooling economics.
questions.placeholder: Reflect on automotive packaging constraints where gearbox casing volume and shaft centre distances (a = 120 mm) are strictly constrained by vehicle underbody packaging. Discuss the trade-offs of induction/case hardening to 400 BHN versus the tooling and casting re-engineering costs of enlarging gear module or gearbox width...

submit.title: Submission & Verification
submit.body: Review your completion status across all 11 activities, verify all calculated checkpoints (torque, pitch diameters, forces, velocity factor, Lewis beam strength, Buckingham wear strength, and engineering recommendation), and submit your official PCC353-MEC CO1 evaluation report.
